finding.claim: /checkout computes the charge total from client-supplied price and qty, letting an authenticated attacker pay 0 or a negative amount.

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty, taken directly from the request body with no server-side price lookup
charge(req.user.id, total) is called with the client-derived total
charged amount is echoed back to the client

finding.guards_checked: No server-side catalog price lookup; no sign or range check on price or qty; no integer or finiteness check on qty; no check that items is a non-empty array. Authentication (req.user) is assumed from middleware not present in this repo. Whether a negative charge credits the account depends on payments.charge, which was not inspected.

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:5 sums i.price * i.qty straight from req.body with no catalog lookup, sign/range check, qty integer check, or array check. cart.js:6 charges that total unconditionally, and cart.js:7 echoes it back. The only other handler in the file, /checkout-v2 (cart.js:13-14), looks up prices via req.catalog.price(i.sku), but it is a separate route and does not guard /checkout. Auth middleware and payments.charge are not in this repo, so they could not be inspected.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: /checkout at cart.js:5-6 charges a total computed entirely from client-supplied price and qty, with no validation in cart.js, so an authenticated customer can submit price 0 or a negative value to set the charge amount. Whether a negative charge credits the account depends on payments.charge, which is outside this repo, but the zero-charge case does not depend on it.

finding.claim: /checkout-v2 does not validate qty or sku, so NaN or Infinity can propagate into the amount passed to charge.

trace.note: p = await req.catalog.price(i.sku); an unknown sku may return undefined or null
total += p * Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)); a missing or non-numeric qty yields NaN, and a huge qty yields Infinity
charge(req.user.id, total) runs with no finiteness check on total

finding.guards_checked: Price comes from the server catalog, so it is not client-controlled. Math.max(1, ...) floors negative and zero quantities to 1. No upper bound on qty, no finiteness check on total, no validation of the catalog price or sku existence. Impact depends on how payments.charge treats NaN and Infinity, which was not inspected.

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:13-14 has no validation of i.sku, i.qty, or the catalog price; cart.js:16 calls charge with total unchecked. No middleware or other files exist in the directory (Glob returned only cart.js), so no upstream validator is visible.
verdict.reason: The trace holds: cart.js:14 yields NaN for a missing or non-numeric qty (Math.max(1, NaN) = NaN) and Infinity for a huge qty, and cart.js:16 passes that total to req.payments.charge unchecked. The attacker is an authenticated user (req.user.id) who can only charge their own account, so the impact is an incorrect self-charge rather than privilege escalation or theft, and the real consequence depends on payments.charge, which is not in the repo.
